title: Sum of Weighted Modes in Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, for every subarray of length k, calculate the mode (the element with the highest frequency, or the smallest element in case of a tie) and its frequency.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, for every subarray of length k, calculate the mode (the element with the highest frequency, or the smallest element in case of a tie) and its frequency. Multiply the mode by its frequency to get the weight. Sum these weights for all subarrays of length k and return the result. A subarray is a continuous segment of the array, and the frequency of an element is the count of its occurrences in the array.
constraints: For each length-k window choose highest frequency, breaking ties by smaller value.
Add mode times its frequency across all windows.
hints: A heap of (-frequency,value) exposes the required mode and tie rule.
Update counts as the window slides and push fresh heap snapshots, discarding stale tops lazily.
Initialize the first window, read its weighted mode, then remove and add one value per shift.
The cleaned heap top always has current maximum frequency and minimum tied value, so every window contributes correctly.
